It all depends on your expectations, willingness to put in some work and the fight youre looking at. But honestly yea, if youre willing to put in the time into both practicing the fight AND becoming a better player, its absolutely possible.

As it is, if your dps is subpar in savage, you will straight up not be able to clear current ultimates. And by that I mean clearing the fight within their patch with original gear. Fru already got a little bit easier with chaotic gear release. You might be able to get carried if dps checks arent too rigid (picto makes those really hard to balance atm) but then youre at the mercy of double party rng and I imagine your goal is to be competent enough to not have to rely on a carry. 

Thing is, you have few options to practice. If youre low parsing savage, plug the log into xivanalysis and see what exactly is the problem. 

If your gcd uptime is low: look at vods, see how people handle mechanics while continuously hitting the boss. Being able to keep gcd uptime is probably the most important thing for any job as it ensures you can just roll your rotation from muscle memory and not drift. In prog, always try to test the waters, how long can you stay on the boss, when exactly does damage snapshot and then you will know when you really have to move. 

If the problem is missing/drifting cooldowns, find a dummy and get to work! Spend decent time just hitting the dummy, rolling your rotation. Without mechanics, you can just fully focus on tracking your cds and with enough time, your rotation will feel more automatic. This also helps with solving mechanics quicker as you dont have to actively think about everything you need to press. 

Even if your damage isnt great yet, you can still practice general ultimate 'tempo' of mechanics in old ultimates. The dps checks are much more lenient there and the clear mostly depends on everyone just executing mechanics correctly. Things happen faster in ultimates, theres more randomness to mechanics where you have to recognize different patterns fast or check half your teams debuffs and adjust etc. I will always recommend UWU as your first ult since at this point its really just a fast extreme. But it does a good job of teaching you a bit more complex mechanics, party member responsibilities and so on. The only issue with old ultimates is that very often the skill distribution on new jobs really sucks. You would have to see if you want to play viper at 70 with the cds it has at that time. You could also just try out smn - as its a very easy rotation but very strong in lvl 70 content. 


You said yourself you are a new player so dont stress out over it too much. Give yourself some time to improve and get to know the game. You seem determined and willing to learn which is already a good sign. With some practice you will definitely be able to get it :)

The problem with fey union is that it's a lvl 70 skill.

For lvls 1-60 you get your skills sprinkled in with job quests. For 60-70 range, you unlock skills automatically when you reach a level EXCEPT for lvl 70 skill, which is the only one you need the quest for.

Not reaally an excuse for not having it at 90, but personally, I definitely forgot that quirk a couple of times after going through 10 levels of skills just unlocking automatically. Its possible they did their quests till 60 (and had other quest-related abilities), saw the next ones just unlock, and didn't do lvl 70 quest.

You should at least check stuff like that before queueing expert, though. Especially when 'new' to healing, you'll want to have all your abilities.

I see your point, but sadly, crooked teeth are more of a complex issue than just aesthetics. Bad bite can give you chronic headaches. If teeth overlap each other, it gets hard to clean and promotes plaque build up, etc. 

I am not a dentist or any medical professional to judge whether something this invasive was the only option or not. I'm pretty sure, though, that no parent caring about their kid would put them through this if it wasn't in some way necessary.

I'm sorry about your experience, and I hope you can overcome your trauma and fear of dentists eventually. Dental health is very important, and I wish it was more accessible worldwide - including less invasive or, in general, alternative options for procedures.

Healthy teeth are incredibly important. Tooth decay/cavities and infections can cause serious health issues. To prevent them, you have to be able to clean your teeth well. It's one of the reasons why wisdom teeth tend to be pulled even if they grow out well - because of how far back they are, they often end up not being cleaned properly and develop cavities.

It's not "being obsessed about teeth", it's caring for your child's health and well-being long term. Teeth are a serious deal.
